acks.detail: Task 1 — the premise that `setsid -f` releases the ssh channel and that `/bin/setsid` is present on the golden image (fleet/RUNBOOK.md:251,370,375; skills/ultrapowers/SKILL.md:30) — tests/test_launch_snippet_detaches.py pins the snippet text and carries the 2026-09-01 probe table (A/E/G 47 s, D/F 2 s) as its docstring, but a documentation test cannot re-measure the orchestrator. A golden image without /bin/setsid would make every documented launch line fail at the shell. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

Task 4 — `readRunbookFromBundle` against a real sandbox bundle (fleet/drive.mjs:199-215, RUNBOOK_MEMBER at :173) — Every `tar -xzOf … --wildcards 'repo/.claude/ultrapowers/run-*/receipt.json'` in fleet/tests/test_drive_pr_runbook.mjs is answered by an exec stub, so no test opens a real archive. The member-name match against what sandboxLogPullCommand (drive.mjs:43-52) actually tars, GNU tar's `--wildcards` availability on the orchestrator, and single-member-ness (two run-* dirs in one bundle would concatenate two JSON documents and degrade to the `post-merge runbook: unreadable` note) are only confirmable on a live drive. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

Task 3 — the rendered `## Rescue` block actually recovers a parked run (fleet/drive.mjs:280-290; fleet/RUNBOOK.md:621-631) — fleet/tests/test_drive_pr_rescue.mjs pins that the four commands render with the run's real ref, tip, branch and host, that unsafe values are refused, and that the RUNBOOK carries the same four verbs — but the ssh fetch from the orchestrator and the operator-credential push are never executed. That the pinned `refs/fleet/<runId>` is reachable over ssh from a laptop is a live-host property. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

Task 7 — the full live `--overlap` chain from drive-one through the sandbox to `ultra_run.py --overlap` (fleet/drive-one.mjs:159, fleet/drive.mjs:1072, fleet/provision.mjs:222, fleet/shim-main.mjs:793) — fleet/tests/test_overlap_threading.mjs pins each of the four hops at its seam (hop 2 aborts at the provision call; hops 3 and 4 stub exec/spawn entirely), so the flag is never carried by a real sandbox into a real engine run. The engine side (`fleet/run-main.mjs` FLAGS['--overlap']) is byte-identical to BASE and untested by this run. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

Task 6 — the runtime goal "none of the three is near 47 s" (fleet/tests/test_drive.mjs, test_drive_evidence.mjs, test_drive_fitness.mjs) — The driver's suite result proves each file exits 0 inside tests/test_fleet_suite.py:26's 120 s subprocess cap, which is the global constraint — but it records no per-file durations, so the split's actual purpose (unpinning the xdist wall from a 46.8 s longest file) is unmeasured. `pytest tests/test_fleet_suite.py -n auto --durations=8` would settle it.
